exclusions.name: ons.savings_interest_income
exclusions.reason: The spine carries £13.8bn of savings interest income against the ONS £95.5bn (-86% at initialization on spine-m, -89% after the solve): the FRS interest income capture, not the weights. Unreachable by reweighting within the stretch bound: a frame-side gap, not a weight question; while bound it pulls the joint solve toward weight concentration (housing benefit alone triples the max/median ratio under grain_equal). One-month window: correct the spine or re-adjudicate.

exclusions.name: obr.housing_benefit
exclusions.reason: The spine carries £2.7bn of housing benefit against the OBR £12.1bn (-78% at initialization on spine-m). Under grain_equal the solver chases the aggregate by multiplying the few HB households (£9.4bn at 512 epochs, £11.4bn at 1500), which halves the effective sample and doubles Glasgow's social-rent count; under uniform it is ignored. Unreachable by reweighting within the stretch bound: a frame-side gap, not a weight question; while bound it pulls the joint solve toward weight concentration (housing benefit alone triples the max/median ratio under grain_equal). One-month window: correct the spine or re-adjudicate.

exclusions.reason: Model concept gap, not a weight question: the engine's carer condition is Carer's Allowance receipt (is_carer_for_benefits = receives_carer_benefit) while the UC carer element needs 35 hours a week of care for a qualifying-benefit recipient with no Carer's Allowance requirement; the spine never fills the engine's care_hours input. Measured at the 10 September 2026 baseline against the bound calendar-2025 paid target: Q50f 595,807 / D2 602,749 paid-UC benefit units against 1,078,514 (-45%). Fitting it would move half the carriers' weight against a definition mismatch. Repair: care hours from the FRS care file and a regulation-based carer condition, then activation.
exclusions.adjudication: microcosm#882 (element sizing at the 10 September 2026 baseline, docs/uk-uc-baseline-2026-09-10.md; María's sign-off in review of microcosm#921 on 2026-09-15, setting the one-month window)

exclusions.name: dwp/uc/elements/childcare
exclusions.reason: Model concept gap, not a weight question: the engine pays the childcare element to every benefit unit where all adults work and childcare costs are reported, with no take-up or incidence lever, while DWP publishes 160-193k households a month receiving it in 2025. Measured at the 10 September 2026 baseline against the bound calendar-2025 target: Q50f 455,634 / D2 451,401 paid-UC benefit units (GBP 2.06bn) against 178,667 published (+155%). Repair: an incidence stage modelled on uc_deduction_attributes drawing to the published count, then activation.

exclusions.name: dwp/uc/elements/housing
exclusions.reason: Structural bias, not a weight question: DWP's any-tenure housing-entitlement count is social plus private plus 'Other or unknown' tenure, and the model has no other/unknown tenure (uc_housing_costs_element pays only council, housing-association and private renters), so the model's any-tenure count is identically the social plus private rows, which are bound and fit; the row overstates the reachable total by the other/unknown cell, 112,518 of 4,037,650 in calendar 2025 (2.8 percent; the published any-tenure mean, which the three tenure cells reproduce to the unit). Fitting all three housing rows would ask the solver to over-fill the tenure rows by that amount. Measured on every evaluation as the housing-element caseload diagnostic (Q50f -0.8 percent, D2 +0.6 percent at the baseline).
